claim: Elaborate behaviours are produced by tightly controlled flexor-extensor motor neuron activation patterns.

claim: Motor neurons are regulated by a network of interneurons within the spinal cord.
source: Motor neurons are regulated by a network of interneurons within the spinal cord, but the computational processes involved in motor control are not fully understood.

claim: The computational processes involved in motor control are not fully understood.
source: Motor neurons are regulated by a network of interneurons within the spinal cord, but the computational processes involved in motor control are not fully understood.

source: The neuroanatomical arrangement of motor and premotor neurons into topographic patterns related to their controlled muscles is thought to facilitate how information is processed by spinal circuits.
evidence: This represents a hypothesis or theoretical framework in the field, based on inference from anatomical organization.

claim: Rabies retrograde monosynaptic tracing has been used to label premotor interneurons innervating specific motor neuron pools.
source: Rabies retrograde monosynaptic tracing has been used to label premotor interneurons innervating specific motor neuron pools, with previous studies reporting topographic mediolateral positional biases in flexor and extensor premotor interneurons.
evidence: This refers to established methodology in the field, citing previous studies.

claim: Previous studies reported topographic mediolateral positional biases in flexor and extensor premotor interneurons.

claim: Multiple complementary viral-tracing approaches in mice were used to minimize systematic biases associated with each method.
source: To more precisely define how premotor interneurons contacting specific motor pools are organized, we used multiple complementary viral-tracing approaches in mice to minimize systematic biases associated with each method.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the current study.

claim: Premotor interneurons contacting motor pools controlling flexion and extension of the ankle are highly intermingled rather than segregated into specific domains like motor neurons.
source: Contrary to expectations, we found that premotor interneurons contacting motor pools controlling flexion and extension of the ankle are highly intermingled rather than segregated into specific domains like motor neurons.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Premotor spinal neurons controlling different muscles process motor instructions in the absence of clear spatial patterns among the flexor-extensor circuit components.
source: Thus, premotor spinal neurons controlling different muscles process motor instructions in the absence of clear spatial patterns among the flexor-extensor circuit components.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claim: In limbed vertebrates, the activity of flexor and extensor muscles is directed by dedicated pools of motor neurons that receive inputs from different subtypes of excitatory and inhibitory interneurons.
source: In limbed vertebrates, the activity of flexor and extensor muscles is directed by dedicated pools of motor neurons that receive inputs from different subtypes of excitatory and inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about vertebrate motor control systems.

claim: Several classes of interneurons have been described in electrophysiological, anatomical, and genetic studies.
source: Several of these classes of interneurons have been described in electrophysiological, anatomical, and genetic studies (Hultborn et al., 1971; Jankowska, 2001; Goulding, 2009); however, the incomplete knowledge of the composition of spinal circuitry that control the activity of flexor and extensor motor neurons limits progress toward a full understanding of motor circuits.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The incomplete knowledge of the composition of spinal circuitry that control the activity of flexor and extensor motor neurons limits progress toward a full understanding of motor circuits.

claim: Rabies virus jumps across synapses in the retrograde direction to infect presynaptic neurons.

evidence: This describes the known behavior of rabies virus, supported by citation.

claim: The use of rabies virus via intramuscular injections led to the identification of polysynaptic pathways.
source: Given that rabies virus (RabV) jumps across synapses in the retrograde direction to infect presynaptic neurons, its use via intramuscular injections led to the identification of polysynaptic pathways (Rathelot and Strick, 2009).

source: Thus, starter cells are generated in one fell swoop by taking advantage of the stringent anatomical specificity of motor neuron to muscle connectivity (Figure 1A).

source: When this method was applied to study the distribution of premotor interneurons controlling the activity of extensor and flexor muscles in the hindlimb, a prominent spatial segregation along the medio-lateral axis of the dorsal ipsilateral spinal cord was observed, with extensor premotor interneurons found in more medial positions than flexors (Tripodi et al., 2011).

source: The distributions of premotor interneurons of LG (6 LG-MG injections, 8 LG-TA injections and 4 single LG injections) and MG (6 LG-MG injections and 4 MG injections) did not reveal any difference in spatial organization (Figure 5A, individual experiments are shown in Figure 12—figure supplements 3 and 4 and Figure 12—figure supplement 6).

evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Single LG or TA injections of ΔG-RabV/mCherry were performed in ChatCre/+; Rosa26RΦGT mice carrying an allele expressing GFP under the control of the neuronal glycine transporter (Slc6A5 or GlyT2) to examine differences in the spatial organization of GlyT2off vs GlyT2on premotor interneurons.
source: Next, we examined whether there are differences in the spatial organization of GlyT2off vs GlyT2on premotor interneurons, where the GlyT2off population will largely comprise excitatory neurons, as well as some purely GABAergic interneurons. We performed single LG or TA injections of ΔG-RabV/mCherry in ChatCre/+; Rosa26RΦGT mice carrying an allele expressing GFP under the control of the neuronal glycine transporter (Slc6A5 or GlyT2; Zeilhofer et al., 2005).
evidence: This describes the experimental design, with citation for the mouse line.

claim: The medians of the medio-lateral position in the dorsal ipsilateral cord for GlyT2off interneurons were 306 μm and 326 μm for LG and TA, respectively (hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.03, IQR –0.08, 0.01).
source: The medians of the medio-lateral position in the dorsal ipsilateral cord were 306 μm and 326 μm for LG and TA, respectively (hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.03, IQR –0.08, 0.01) and –112 μm and 74 μm (hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.14, IQR −0.24,–0.04) in the ventral spinal cord (Figure 6B–C).

claim: No segregation was observed in the distribution of GlyT2on LG and TA premotor interneurons.
source: Similarly, we did not observe segregation in the distribution of GlyT2on LG and TA premotor interneurons (Figure 6D).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figure 6D.

claim: The medians of the medio-lateral coordinates of the dorsal GlyT2on interneurons were 303 μm for LG and 346 μm for TA (hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.30, IQR −0.35,–0.24).
source: The medians of the medio-lateral coordinates of the dorsal GlyT2on interneurons were 303 μm for LG and 346 μm for TA (hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.30, IQR −0.35,–0.24), while for ventral interneurons were 395 μm for LG and 437 μm for TA (hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.33, IQR –0.40, 0.27, Figure 6E–F).

claim: There is no significant difference in the distribution of GlyT2off and GlyT2on premotor interneurons controlling the activity of flexor and extensor muscles.
source: These data indicate that there is no significant difference in the distribution of GlyT2off and GlyT2on premotor interneurons controlling the activity of flexor and extensor muscles.

source: No differences were observed for the medio-lateral distribution of inhibitory and excitatory dorsal premotor interneurons (medians for LG: GlyT2on = 303 μm and GlyT2off = 306 μm; hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=–0.06, IQR 0.03, 0.09. Medians for TA: GlyT2on = 346 and GlyT2off = 326 μm; hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=0.15, IQR 0.08, 0.23).
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Ventral ipsilateral GlyT2on were more abundant than GlyT2off for both LG and TA.
source: In contrast, ventral ipsilateral GlyT2on were more abundant than GlyT2off for both LG (Figure 6H–I) and TA (Figure 6K–L).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figures 6H-I and 6K-L.

claim: GlyT2off premotor interneurons dominated the ventral contralateral side.
source: Conversely, GlyT2off premotor interneurons dominated the ventral contralateral side (Figure 6H and K; medians for LG: GlyT2off = –112 μm and GlyT2on = 395 μm; hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=0.72, IQR 0.61, 0.84. Medians for TA: GlyT2off = 74 μm and GlyT2on = 437 μm; hierarchical bootstrapped Hedges'G=0.91, IQR 0.82, 0.99).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figures 6H and K.

claim: There is a clear segregation in the distributions of GlyT2off and GlyT2on premotor interneurons in the ventral half of the spinal cord: GlyT2on interneurons are almost exclusively found in the ipsilateral side while GlyT2off interneurons also present a prominent peak in the contralateral side.
source: Overall, the data show a clear segregation in the distributions of GlyT2off and GlyT2on premotor interneurons in the ventral half of the spinal cord: GlyT2on interneurons are almost exclusively found in the ipsilateral side while GlyT2off interneurons also present a prominent peak in the contralateral side (Figure 6G–L).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data, illustrated in Figures 6G-L.

claim: While the study is able to detect significant differences in the positional organization of premotor interneurons with different transmitter phenotype, the organization of flexor and extensor premotor circuits were always intermingled regardless of their neurotransmitter status.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that while we are able to detect significant differences in the positional organization of premotor interneurons with different transmitter phenotype, we found that the organization of flexor and extensor premotor circuits were always intermingled regardless of their neurotransmitter status.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ChatCre/+ is not only expressed in motor neurons but also cholinergic interneurons, including medial partition cells (V0c neurons) that have prominent projections to motor neurons.
source: In the spinal cord, ChatCre/+ is not only expressed in motor neurons but also cholinergic interneurons, including medial partition cells (V0c neurons) that have prominent projections to motor neurons (Zagoraiou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Cre line, supported by citation.

claim: Given that under the experimental conditions, V0c neurons express G and are presynaptic to motor neurons, they could permit disynaptic rabies transfer: first from motor neurons to V0c neurons and second from V0c neurons to their presynaptic partners.
source: Therefore, given that under our experimental conditions, V0c neurons express G and are presynaptic to motor neurons, they could permit disynaptic rabies transfer: first from motor neurons to V0c neurons and second from V0c neurons to their presynaptic partners.
evidence: This is an inference about a potential confound in the experimental design.

claim: V0c presynaptic partners have been previously characterised using rabies monosynaptic tracing and comprise many interneurons (and/or axonal arborisations) located in the dorsal laminae of the spinal cord, an area that is largely devoid of rabies labelling in the current experiments.
source: However, it is important to note that V0c presynaptic partners have been previously characterised using rabies monosynaptic tracing and comprise many interneurons (and/or axonal arborisations) located in the dorsal laminae of the spinal cord (Zampieri et al., 2014), an area that is largely devoid of rabies labelling in our experiments.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research, with inference about its relevance to the current study.

claim: A set of experiments (4 gastrocnemius, GS and 3 TA injections) were performed using the Olig2Cre/+ instead of the ChatCre/+ line to test whether disynaptic transfer from premotor interneurons is affecting the analysis.
source: In order to test whether disynaptic transfer from premotor interneurons is affecting our analysis, we performed a set of experiments (4 gastrocnemius, GS and 3 TA injections) using the Olig2Cre/+ (Dessaud et al., 2007) instead of the ChatCre/+ line (Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes the experimental design, with citation for the mouse line and reference to Figure 1E.

claim: The Olig2Cre/+ line would ensure recombination in motor neurons but not in V0c or other cholinergic interneurons.
source: This line would ensure recombination in motor neurons but not in V0c or other cholinergic interneurons.
evidence: This is an inference about the specificity of the Cre line.

claim: Olig2 is transiently expressed during embryonic development in subsets of p2 and p3 progenitors.
source: However, Olig2 is transiently expressed during embryonic development in subsets of p2 and p3 progenitors (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Olig2 gene, supported by citation.

claim: If additional transsynaptic transfer from premotor interneurons is significantly affecting the results, using a different Cre line to drive G expression in a non-overlapping subset of premotor interneurons should result in different labelling patterns.
source: We reasoned that if additional transsynaptic transfer from premotor interneurons is significantly affecting our results, using a different Cre line to drive G expression in a non-overlapping subset of premotor interneurons should result in different labelling patterns.
evidence: This is the reasoning behind the experimental design.

claim: Six days following injection in Olig2Cre/+; Rosa26RΦGT mice, interneuron labelling was observed with a pattern similar to that of those performed in ChatCre/+ mice.
source: Six days following injection, we observed interneuron labelling with a pattern similar to that of those performed in ChatCre/+ mice (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figures 7A-B.

claim: There was no difference in the positional organization of flexor and extensor premotor interneurons in the transverse plane in Olig2Cre/+; Rosa26RΦGT mice.
source: There was no difference in the positional organization of flexor and extensor premotor interneurons in the transverse plane (Figure 7C–E individual experiments are shown in Figure 12—figure supplements 11–12) as well as along the rostro-caudal axis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), with median values along the mediolateral axis of 295 μm for GS and 310 μm for TA (bootstrapped Hedges' G=–0.02, IQR –0.07, 0.03).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figures 7C-E, Figure 12—figure supplements 11–12, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Comparison of the premotor maps obtained from ChatCre/+ and Olig2Cre/+ experiments showed that interneuron distributions were indistinguishable, as shown by the high correlation values across mouse lines and muscles (r>0.9) and the low values of hierarchical bootstraps of the Hedges' G coefficients.
source: Comparison of the premotor maps obtained from ChatCre/+ and Olig2Cre/+ experiments showed that interneuron distributions were indistinguishable, as shown by the high correlation values across mouse lines and muscles (r>0.9) and the low values of hierarchical bootstraps of the Hedges' G coefficients across muscles and Olig2Cre/+ and ChatCre/+ injections (Figure 7F).
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data, illustrated in Figure 7F.

claim: The median interneuron positions along the medio-lateral axis for each experiment were similar between ChatCre/+ (322 μm for GS and 315 μm for TA) and Olig2Cre/+ (295 μm for GS and 310 μm for TA) animals injected in the same muscle.
source: In addition, the median interneuron positions along the medio-lateral axis for each experiment were similar between ChatCre/+ (322 μm for GS and 315 μm for TA, including high and low efficiency experiments) and Olig2Cre/+ (295 μm for GS and 310 μm for TA) animals injected in the same muscle (Figure 7G, Hedges' G=0.14 (IQR 0.09, 0.18) for GS pairs and 0.13 (IQR 0.08, 0.18) for TA pairs).
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data, illustrated in Figure 7G.

claim: Under the experimental conditions, the results of tracing experiments done in ChatCre/+; Rosa26RΦGT and Olig2Cre/+; Rosa26RΦGT mice are unlikely to be influenced by disynaptic rabies transfer from spinal premotor interneurons.
source: Thus, these results indicate that under our experimental conditions the results of tracing experiments done in ChatCre/+; Rosa26RΦGT and Olig2Cre/+; Rosa26RΦGT mice are unlikely to be influenced by disynaptic rabies transfer from spinal premotor interneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: In contrast to previous findings using AAV-G, extensive intermingling of flexor and extensor premotor interneurons was found when using Cre-based methods to genetically express G-protein in order to complement rabies replication.
source: In contrast to previous findings using AAV-G (Tripodi et al., 2011), we found extensive intermingling of flexor and extensor premotor interneurons when using Cre-based methods to genetically express G-protein in order to complement rabies replication (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding, with citation to previous work and reference to Figures 1D and E.

claim: The authors sought to replicate the previous findings using AAV-G complementation strategies.
source: Therefore, we sought to replicate the previous findings using AAV-G complementation strategies (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This describes the experimental design, with reference to Figures 1A and B.

source: We first performed injections of 1 μl of a 3:1 AAV-G: ΔG-RabV mixture in GS and TA muscles of P2 wild-type mice (Figure 1A; Tripodi et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure, with citation and reference to Figure 1A.

source: Ten days following injection, consistent labelling with both viruses was observed throughout the lumbar region (L1: Figure 8A and L: Figure 8B).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figures 8A and 8B.

source: Analysis of rabies-labelled interneurons did not reveal any apparent difference in the distributions of premotor circuits controlling the activity of antagonist muscles in the transverse plane as well as along the rostro-caudal axis (Figure 8C, individual experiments are shown in Figure 12—figure supplement 13).

source: The Hedges' G coefficients of premotor interneuron distributions in the ipsilateral dorsal quadrant for all the experiments had a median of –0.02 (IQR –0.29, 0.28), indicating high uniformity across experiments, as also shown by the high correlation values of positional coordinates of flexor and extensor interneurons (Figure 8D).

claim: Findings obtained using AAV-G complementation are consistent with the pattern of premotor interneuron mixing identified using genetic-delivery of G-protein.
source: These findings obtained using AAV-G complementation are therefore consistent with the pattern of premotor interneuron mixing identified using genetic-delivery of G-protein.

source: In these AAV-G complementation experiments, we observed extensive labelling of superficial dorsal interneurons, a feature that was absent when using genetic complementation methods (compare Figure 8C with 3 C, 4 C, and 7E).
evidence: This describes an observation from comparing experimental results across different methods, illustrated in multiple figures.

claim: Contribution of transsynaptic transfer from sensory afferents, precluded by genetic complementation approaches, may result in tracing of dorsal and medial interneurons and thus affect analysis of premotor circuits.
source: We therefore reasoned that contribution of transsynaptic transfer from sensory afferents, precluded by our genetic complementation approaches, may result in tracing of dorsal and medial interneurons and thus affect analysis of premotor circuits (Zampieri et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference about a potential confound, supported by citation.

source: To test this idea, we restricted expression of G to motor neurons by injecting AAV-flex-optimizedG (oG, Kim et al., 2016) in GS and TA muscles of ChatCre/+ mice (1 μl of a 3:1 AAV-flex-oG: ΔG-RabV mix), a strategy that was previously used to show segregation of flexor and extensor premotor circuits (Figure 1B; Wang et al., 2017).

claim: In AAV-flex-oG experiments (4 GS and 3 TA injections), the distributions of GS and TA premotor interneurons were similar.
source: In these experiments (4 GS and 3 TA injections), the distributions of GS and TA premotor interneurons were similar (Figure 9A–C, individual experiments are shown in Figure 12—figure supplements 14–15), with high correlation values across experiments (Figure 9D).
evidence: This describes experimental results, illustrated in Figures 9A-C, 9D, and Figure 12—figure supplements 14–15.

claim: Analysis of the medio-lateral positioning in the ipsilateral dorsal quadrant showed that the median position of TA related interneurons was shifted by only 33 μm with respect to that of the GS related interneurons, and that this was in a medial direction (383 μm for GS and 350 μm for TA; Hedges' G from hierarchical bootstrap = –0.15, IQR −0.24, –0.05).
source: Analysis of the medio-lateral positioning in the ipsilateral dorsal quadrant showed that the median position of TA related interneurons was shifted by only 33 μm with respect to that of the GS related interneurons, and that this was in a medial direction (383 μm for GS and 350 μm for TA; Hedges' G from hierarchical bootstrap = –0.15, IQR −0.24, –0.05, Figure 9E and F).
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data, illustrated in Figures 9E and F.

claim: Regardless of whether the expression of G was restricted to motor neurons or not, no differences were observed in the mediolateral position of dorsal ipsilateral premotor interneurons related to flexor or extensor muscles.
source: Regardless of whether the expression of G was restricted to motor neurons (Figure 9) or not (Figure 8), we observed no differences in the mediolateral position of dorsal ipsilateral premotor interneurons related to flexor or extensor muscles.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing experimental results, with reference to Figures 8 and 9.

claim: The use of AAV-oG-Flex that prevents anterograde jumps by restricting G expression to motor neurons led to important differences compared to AAV-G.
source: However, the use of AAV-oG-Flex that, contrarily to AAV-G, prevents anterograde jumps by restricting G expression to motor neurons (Figure 1A–B), led to important differences.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing experimental results, with reference to Figures 1A-B.

claim: Experiments using AAV-G result in an extensive labelling of superficial dorsal horn neurons for both tested muscles.
source: Indeed, despite being performed and analysed by the same lab at similar timepoints for injection (P1-P2) and harvesting (7–8 days post-injection), experiments using AAV-G result in an extensive labelling of superficial dorsal horn neurons for both tested muscles (Figure 10A).

claim: The median values along the dorsoventral axis were 249 and 375 μm for GS and 295 and 344 μm for TA following AAV-G or AAV-Flex-oG injections respectively.
source: The median values along the dorsoventral axis were 249 and 375 μm for GS and 295 and 344 μm for TA following AAV-G or AAV-Flex-oG injections respectively.
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data.

source: The Hedges' G bootstrapped coefficients were –0.55 (IQR −0.64,–0.46) for the GS pairs and –0.14 (IQR −0.23,–0.08) for the TA pairs.
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data.

source: In addition, there was an excess of medially located infected neurons, in both GS and TA experiments, when the expression of G was not restricted to motor neurons.
evidence: This describes an observation from experimental data.

source: The dorsoventral and mediolateral differences in the distributions observed in AAV-G and AAV-oG-Flex experiments were substantial for both GS and TA, thus indicating that when G could be expressed by sensory neurons (AAV-G muscle injection), the average position of labelled cells extended more dorsally and medially compared to experiments in which G could only be expressed in motor neurons (AAV-oG-Flex).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing experimental data.

claim: The observed mediodorsal shift is compatible with a contribution of anterograde tracing from sensory neurons, which is absent when G is restricted to motor neurons.
source: The observed mediodorsal shift is compatible with a contribution of anterograde tracing from sensory neurons (Figure 10A–C), which is absent when G is restricted to motor neurons, either by using AAV-oG-Flex, or by genetic restrictions.
evidence: This is an inference about the cause of observed differences, illustrated in Figures 10A-C.

claim: Regardless of the possible effects derived from anterograde tracing, the distributions of labelled cells observed in flexor and extensor experiments did not differ.
source: Nonetheless, regardless of the possible effects derived from anterograde tracing, the distributions of labelled cells observed in flexor and extensor experiments did not differ.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

source: Pseudorabies virus (PRV) is a neurotropic virus that travels transsynaptically in the retrograde direction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PRV.

source: Accordingly, the medians of mediolateral positions of flexor and extensor premotor interneurons were similar (353 μm for GS and 366 μm for TA; Figure 11E and F).

claim: In all cases, the correlations between flexor and extensor muscles labelled with the same methods were very high.

source: The lowest correlation coefficients (which were still high) were typically observed between experiments with AAV-G injection in wild type mice and all the other methods, regardless of the muscle injected, consistent with a substantial contamination from interneurons anterogradely labelled through sensory afferents.

claim: The medians of the mediolateral positions did not differ between muscles for any of the methods used.
source: Overall, the medians of the mediolateral positions (Figure 12B) did not differ between muscles for any of the methods used and the range of bootstrapped Hedges' G coefficient was between –0.23 and 0.17 across pairs of antagonist muscles throughout five different experimental paradigms tested.
evidence: This describes statistical analysis of experimental data, illustrated in Figure 12B.

claim: Premotor interneurons innervating flexor and extensor motor neurons are not spatially segregated.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that premotor interneurons innervating flexor and extensor motor neurons are not spatially segregated.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on all the experimental data.
